topic: What happens if you go to space without a suit?
title: Space Without A Suit
hook: Could you survive space without a suit?

beats.label: 1 SECOND
beats.line: First, breathe out. Holding your breath could tear your lungs.

beats.label: 5 SECONDS
beats.line: The water on your tongue starts to boil, but your blood doesn't.

beats.label: 10 SECONDS
beats.line: Your skin swells up, but you don't explode like in the movies.

beats.label: 15 SECONDS
beats.line: With no oxygen reaching your brain, you black out.

beats.label: 90 SECONDS
beats.line: Pulled back inside within about ninety seconds, you could still survive.

end.line: Did you think you would explode?

description: No explosion, no frozen statue: the real first seconds in space without a suit.

facts.claim: You should exhale; holding your breath in a vacuum can rupture the lungs.
facts.source: NASA - Ask an Astrophysicist: human body in a vacuum

facts.claim: Saliva on the tongue boils in a vacuum (Jim LeBlanc, NASA vacuum chamber accident, 1966).
Blood in the vessels does not boil because the body keeps it under pressure.
facts.source: NASA - Human body in a vacuum

facts.claim: The skin and tissues swell, but the body does not explode.
facts.source: NASA - Human body in a vacuum

facts.claim: Consciousness lasts about 15 seconds; animal studies showed survival after up to about 90 seconds.
facts.source: NASA Technical Report - Bioastronautics Data Book
